entities.name: IOS
entities.rationale: iOS mobile client application accessing backend microservices.

entities.name: ANDROID
entities.rationale: Android mobile client application receiving notifications/responses from MCS.

entities.name: EKS
entities.rationale: Amazon EKS cluster enclosing GW, MEDIA, MCS, FRIEND GRAPH, and SNAP DB microservices.

entities.name: GW
entities.rationale: API Gateway routing incoming mobile client traffic inside the EKS cluster.

entities.name: MEDIA
entities.rationale: Media processing microservice running on EKS cluster.

entities.name: MCS
entities.rationale: Messaging/Core Service microservice running on EKS cluster.

entities.name: FRIEND GRAPH
entities.rationale: Friend Graph microservice managing user social graphs inside EKS.

entities.name: SNAP DB
entities.rationale: Snap DB microservice handling transient metadata before persisting into DynamoDB.

entities.name: CLOUDFRONT
entities.rationale: Amazon CloudFront content delivery network distributing static and media assets.

entities.name: S3
entities.rationale: Amazon S3 bucket serving as origin storage for media content.

entities.name: ELASTICACHE
entities.rationale: Amazon ElastiCache in-memory cache layer used by MCS for low-latency state retrieval.

entities.name: DYNAMODB
entities.rationale: Amazon DynamoDB table storing persistent data (400TB, 2B+/min).

visual_connections.description: iOS client sends request traffic into the API Gateway.
API Gateway routes media-related traffic to the MEDIA microservice.
API Gateway routes messaging requests to the MCS microservice.
MEDIA microservice pushes or requests media delivery through CloudFront.
CloudFront fetches original media files stored in Amazon S3.
MCS microservice queries user relationship data from the FRIEND GRAPH microservice.
MCS microservice writes ephemeral snap data into SNAP DB service.
MCS microservice reads and writes session state to ElastiCache.
MCS delivers push notifications or responses to Android mobile clients.
SNAP DB persists high-volume transaction records to Amazon DynamoDB.
